newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Leotard to fight National Front in south.
newsitem.headline: France's Leotard to fight National Front in south.

text.p: Centre-right former French defence minister Francois Leotard declared war on the extreme-right National Front on Thursday, saying he would stand against the movement in its Riviera bastion in regional elections next year.

Leotard, leader of the Union for French Democracy (UDF), junior partner in the governing coalition, told the conservative daily Le Figaro he would run in the Var district, where the Front controls the naval port of Toulon.
"The National Front is a xenophobic, antisemitic and crypto-fascist movement," he said.

Leotard, 54, a potential presidential candidate, said he had taken his decision after the anti-immigration party conquered a fourth southern French town in a municipal election in Vitrolles, near Marseille, on Sunday.
"The Vitrolles election and the general trend in the region are driving me to get physically involved in the political fight beyond my own municipality (of Frejus)," he said.
"You can't remain indifferent or simply walk away from this sort of fight."

Political analysts say the National Front, led by Jean-Marie Le Pen, could become the biggest group in the Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur regional assembly due to the strict proportional representation system used for regional elections.

The region features all the conditions that favour the extreme-right -- pockets of high unemployment, poorly integrated North African immigrants, a large concentration of former French settlers from Algeria, a high crime rate and political corruption among the mainstream parties.
